chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whom beasts and birds have eaten, and only his bones remain without flesh—how should he be dealt with? He said: “He should be given ghusl (ritual washing), shrouded, the funeral prayer should be performed over him, and he should be buried. If the deceased is in two halves, the prayer is performed over the half in which the heart is present.”

key_terms.السَّبُعُ: a predatory beast that has consumed part of the body
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: birds that have eaten from the deceased body
key_terms.الْقَلْبُ: the heart, used here to identify the half over which prayer is offered
key_terms.عِظَامُهُ: his bones remaining after the flesh is gone
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: the funeral prayer is to be performed over him
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he is to be given ghusl (ritual washing) for the deceased
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: he is to be shrouded in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: How should funeral rites be performed for a body that has been partially eaten or divided?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the treatment of human remains when the body has been partially consumed and only bones remain. It establishes that the deceased is still to be given ghusl (ritual washing), shrouding, funeral prayer, and burial, and if the body is divided into two parts, salat is performed over the half containing the heart.
